reason: Both conversations issued the correct 'stop using' safety warning at the outset, but Conversation 2 stopped there with a single generic message and never engaged with the homeowner's situation, asked about the nature or location of the smell, or gave escalation guidance. Conversation 1 asked the right diagnostic questions, elicited the key facts (electrical/plastic smell from rear, warm discoloured cooker switch), correctly identified an overheating supply connection/switch as the likely cause while acknowledging the terminal block as an alternative, told them not to remove the switch faceplate or panels, advised isolating at the consumer unit, and escalated to an electrician/engineer with no unjustified part recommendation. Conversation 1's first reply was somewhat over-long and its 'most likely' framing slightly overstates certainty, but it clearly served the homeowner better.
